evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle-bone examples and cited inscriptions
evidence.text: The entry describes 日 as a depiction of the sun, says the graph could be squared because circles were difficult to carve on bone, and says its central mark distinguished it from 囗. It cites Shang oracle-bone examples for the sun and sunrise (合集34163), eclipse (合集11480), daylight contrasted with evening (合集33871, 合集34036), a five-day period (合集12314), and a sacrificial name (合集27463). The entry documents these uses but does not establish their relative chronology or the semantic links between them.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：日

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, digitized 說文解字 with 段玉裁 commentary
evidence.field: 卷七 日部 entry and commentary
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry defines 日 as 實, describes it as 太陽之精不虧, segments it as 从囗一, and calls it pictographic. Duan Yucai interprets the outer shape as the sun's outline and the inner stroke as its undiminished center. This is a historical lexicographic analysis, not direct evidence for the graph's earliest form.
evidence.title: 說文解字「日」

evidence.field: File description; image identity, provenance, and reuse rights
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 日-bigseal.svg as a modern Inkscape vector depiction of 日 in Liushutong script style and gives public-domain status for the representation. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The page's Original file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6b/%E6%97%A5-bigseal.svg; opening that direct image URL returned a cache-miss access failure in this run.

gaps: CUHK cites Shang-period oracle-bone catalogue identifiers for several uses but does not provide verified dates for each inscription here. Treat these as Shang-period attestations, not securely dated first occurrences.

The cited evidence does not establish whether sun, daylight, day-unit, or sacrificial-name uses arose first, nor does it establish all semantic links among them. Dictionary gloss order is not chronology.

The early graph is interpreted as a sun depiction. The received Shuowen segmentation 从囗一 is not independently established by the earlier inscriptional evidence as the graph's original component structure.
The official Unihan character-specific lookup failed; the local kMandarin row is not emitted as externally verified evidence.
